note: Live capability state for issue #5423, Codex cells re-probed on 2026-10-20 with codex-cli 0.163.0 on the ChatGPT subscription login (OPENAI_API_KEY, CODEX_API_KEY, and OPENAI_BASE_URL unset); Copilot cells are from GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.89 (probed 2026-09-24) and Copilot is dropped from eval support. The Codex pin tracks the installed CLI: a codex auto-update invalidates it, and every Codex cell must then be re-probed before a run. scripts/eval/examples/harness-capability-probes.json holds the single-agent override plan; the topology, isolation, and handoff probes are recorded per cell. Every VERIFIED cell cites a trimmed backend capture under tests/eval/fixtures/harness_capability/, and tests/eval/test_harness_capability_live_evidence.py re-derives each VERIFIED cell from that capture. Codex backend model and effort come from websocket response frames logged with RUST_LOG=tungstenite::protocol=trace; codex --json stdout carries neither. GitHub-routed Copilot calls returned HTTP 402 (monthly quota exceeded), so Copilot behavioral cells were probed through the documented BYOK Anthropic provider and GitHub-routed Sol, Luna, and Terra models remain unobserved. VERIFIED is reserved for backend evidence only. Provider/model/pricing authority stays in scripts/eval/_providers.py and scripts/eval/_eval_common.py; supported_models here is the observed-live set, not a registry. On 2026-10-03 the owner dropped Copilot from eval support, so no Copilot live probe is owed and its cells stay as last observed. Earlier Codex captures (codex-0.157.1 and codex-0.160.0 under tests/eval/fixtures/harness_capability/) are history: this matrix pins 0.163.0 and every Codex cell cites a codex-0.163.0 capture. Claude Code cells were probed on 2026-10-23 with claude 2.1.309 on the operator's stored claude.ai subscription login (system/init apiKeySource none; ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, and the Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry switches removed). The CLI auto-updated from 2.1.307 to 2.1.309 during the session, so the pin is 2.1.309 and the runner sets DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER. Claude is standalone: results per harness are never pooled, so it is no peer for Codex and Codex is none for it. Claude stream-json names the served model on every assistant message and names no reasoning effort, so effort_override stays UNVERIFIED. Claude effort rests on behavioral evidence (Amendment 4, D12): per-model thinking-token counts in effort_behavioral, valid for the claude harness only.

harnesses.tool_sandbox_constraints: Sandbox is chosen per run with -s read-only, workspace-write, or danger-full-access; the plan writer needed workspace-write and every other probe ran read-only. The collaboration tools (spawn_agent, wait_agent, send_message, followup_task, interrupt_agent, list_agents) are sent on every request, even with --disable multi_agent --disable multi_agent_v2 or -c agents.max_threads=1, so no-child execution is by instruction and is checked per run, not enforced. spawn_agent fork_turns defaults to all; fork_turns=all needs a persisted thread and fails under --ephemeral with 'collab spawn failed: no thread with id'. An isolated CODEX_HOME given CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN from a ChatGPT login is rejected with 401 (codex-0.156.0/isolated-auth-401.stdout.jsonl), so the isolated profile in eval_harness_capability.py needs CODEX_API_KEY. Backend model and effort appear only in RUST_LOG=tungstenite::protocol=trace frames on stderr.
harnesses.failure_retry_behavior: On a 401 Codex emitted 'Reconnecting... n/5' error events for 5 websocket attempts, fell back to HTTPS, retried 5 more times, then emitted turn.failed and exited 1 (codex-0.156.0/isolated-auth-401.stdout.jsonl). A benchmark must count that as one failed invocation. No cost field and no elapsed-time field appear in --json output; elapsed time is only derivable from trace-line timestamps.

Top-level -m gpt-5.6-terra reports gpt-5.6-terra and -m gpt-5.6-luna reports gpt-5.6-luna. Each subagent must reply with only its index number (1, 2, or 3). Wait for all three, then reply with the three answers joined by commas. Do not run shell commands.'

concurrency_limit.detail: With agents.max_threads=3, 3 children ran at once and 2 further spawn(s) were refused. The parent waited, so every child closed its turn. Derived from codex-0.163.0/concurrency-cap3-wait.parent.rollout.jsonl and its 3 child rollouts by eval_recorded_capabilities.py. A parent that does not wait ends its children in turn_aborted and yields no ceiling (codex-0.163.0/concurrency-cap3-nowait.parent.rollout.jsonl), so every benchmark parent must wait. Without a cap, 3 requested gpt-5.6-luna children overlapped at a peak of 3 (codex-0.163.0/concurrency-3-requested.trace.log); the 0.160.0 capture, which requested gpt-6-luna children, peaked at 1, so a requested fan-out is not serialized and agents.max_threads is the only ceiling. With agents.max_threads=1 the second spawn was refused (codex-0.163.0/thread-limit-1.stdout.jsonl).
concurrency_limit.probe_command: RUST_LOG=tungstenite::protocol=trace codex exec --json --skip-git-repo-check --ignore-user-config --ignore-rules -c agents.max_threads=3 -s read-only -m gpt-5.6-sol -c model_reasoning_effort=low 'Spawn 5 subagents one after another with fork_turns none, each told to write 300 words about a river and then reply with its index. Do not wait on any before spawning all 5. Reply with each spawn result or the exact spawn error. Then wait for every spawned child to finish before you reply.' ; then: python3 scripts/eval/eval_recorded_capabilities.py --captures scripts/eval/examples/harness-capability-recorded-captures-0.163.0.json

reviewer_isolation.detail: The parent held the private word ZEBRA-7731. A reviewer spawned with fork_turns=none answered NONE, and the positive control spawned with fork_turns=all answered ZEBRA-7731. Isolation therefore requires an explicit fork_turns=none, because the default fork_turns=all leaks producer context. Evidence: codex-0.163.0/reviewer-isolation.trace.log.
reviewer_isolation.probe_command: RUST_LOG=tungstenite::protocol=trace codex exec --json --skip-git-repo-check --ignore-user-config --ignore-rules -s read-only -m gpt-5.6-sol -c model_reasoning_effort=medium 'Producer-private code word: ZEBRA-7731. Never write this code word in any spawn_agent message. Step 1: spawn a subagent with task_name reviewer_none, fork_turns "none", no model override, message: '"'"'If any code word of the form WORD-NNNN appears anywhere in your context, reply with it exactly; otherwise reply NONE.'"'"' Wait for it. Step 2: spawn a subagent with task_name reviewer_all, fork_turns "all", no model override, with the same message. Wait for it. If a spawn fails, include the exact error text. Then reply with: none=<first answer> all=<second answer>. Do not run shell commands.'

sol_ultra.detail: Not verified as a distinct tier. Control: -c model_reasoning_effort=ultra on gpt-6-sol or gpt-5.6-sol. The codex-cli 0.163.0 backend model catalog lists ultra for gpt-6-sol, gpt-6-astra, gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-5.6-sol, and gpt-5.6-terra, not for gpt-6-luna or gpt-5.6-luna, and describes it as 'Maximum reasoning with automatic task delegation'. For an ultra request the backend response.created frame reports reasoning.effort max and mode standard, so the effort field the backend reports for ultra is max, and ultra is never aliased to max here. Whether ultra also changes delegation behavior was not observed. Evidence: codex-0.163.0/sol-6-ultra.trace.log, codex-0.163.0/sol-5.6-ultra.trace.log, codex-0.163.0/models-catalog.json.

harnesses.tool_sandbox_constraints: GitHub-routed calls all returned HTTP 402 (monthly quota exceeded), so every behavioral cell below was probed through the documented BYOK path: COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic with the Anthropic API. BYOK replaces GitHub model routing, so GitHub-routed gpt-6/gpt-5.6 models (Sol, Luna, Terra) remain unobserved. The provider's own response, including its model id, appears only in the debug log written by --log-level all --log-dir <dir> as '[rust:model_wire] response (Request-ID ...)'. --excluded-tools task removes the subagent tool. --allow-all-tools, --allow-tool, --deny-tool, --available-tools, --allow-all-paths, and --disallow-temp-dir also exist (copilot --help, 1.0.89).

effort_override.detail: Not verified for every model. The stream never names a reasoning effort, so the owner accepted behavioral evidence for Claude (D12, Amendment 4): a model's effort control is verified when its thinking tokens strictly increase across low, medium, and high on one fixed prompt, one claude -p call per level, on the pinned CLI. Measured thinking tokens (low, medium, high), one call each on 2.1.309: claude-opus-5-5 100, 106, 134 (strictly increasing, verified); claude-sonnet-5-5 105, 103, 105 (inversion and tie, not verified); claude-haiku-5-5 285, 233, 337 (inversion, not verified). Fixtures: claude-2.1.309/effort-opus-low.stdout.jsonl, claude-2.1.309/effort-opus-medium.stdout.jsonl, claude-2.1.309/effort-opus-high.stdout.jsonl, claude-2.1.309/effort-sonnet-low.stdout.jsonl, claude-2.1.309/effort-sonnet-medium.stdout.jsonl, claude-2.1.309/effort-sonnet-high.stdout.jsonl, claude-2.1.309/effort-haiku-low.stdout.jsonl, claude-2.1.309/effort-haiku-medium.stdout.jsonl, claude-2.1.309/effort-haiku-high.stdout.jsonl. The cell stays UNVERIFIED because two of three models fail, and the arm gate reads the per-model counts, so an arm that needs only claude-opus-5-5 is eligible. The rule shows the flag changes behavior, never which value was served. An earlier haiku low and max pair read 73 and 279 (claude-2.1.309/effort-low.stdout.jsonl, claude-2.1.309/effort-max.stdout.jsonl) and is not part of the rule. An unknown value is ignored, not refused: --effort ultra warned on stderr, ran at the default effort, and exited 0 (claude-2.1.309/effort-ultra-ignored.stdout.jsonl, claude-2.1.309/effort-ultra-ignored.stderr.txt).

subagent_support.detail: The parent issued an Agent tool call (listed as Task in system/init tools) with subagent_type worker. Forwarded child messages carry parent_tool_use_id, and the result subagent_stats read spawned 1, completed 1, by_type worker 1 (claude-2.1.309/subagent-haiku-child.stdout.jsonl). The routing runner never uses this: each runner invocation is its own claude process whose --tools list omits the Agent tool, so fan-out is the runner's.

concurrency_limit.detail: With CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS=3 a parent asked for 5 workers at once. Workers 1 to 3 launched and ran in the background, worker 1 finished and worker 4 launched, and the call for worker 5 was refused with 'Concurrent subagent limit reached. You can run 3 subagents at once.', and the final subagent_stats read refused.concurrency_limit 1 (claude-2.1.309/concurrency-cap3.stdout.jsonl). Without the variable the same request ran 5 workers with refused.concurrency_limit 0 (claude-2.1.309/concurrency-uncapped.stdout.jsonl). The control is an environment variable, not a flag. The runner does not set it and never overlaps its own invocations, so a runner row peaks at concurrency 1.
concurrency_limit.probe_command: claude -p <prompt> --model claude-opus-5-5 --effort low --permission-mode acceptEdits --agents '{"worker":{"description":"...","prompt":"...","model":"claude-haiku-5-5","tools":[]}}' --setting-sources '' --strict-mcp-config --disable-slash-commands --no-session-persistence --output-format stream-json --verbose --forward-subagent-text  # env CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS=3

parent_child_override.detail: In one run the parent's assistant messages name claude-opus-5-5 and the child's name claude-haiku-5-5, and the result modelUsage lists both ids, so the child did not inherit the parent's model (claude-2.1.309/subagent-haiku-child.stdout.jsonl). A child effort override cannot be observed for the reason given under effort_override.

reviewer_isolation.detail: The parent held the private word ZEBRA-7731 in its own prompt. A reviewer subagent whose prompt did not contain it answered NONE, and a control subagent whose prompt did contain it answered ZEBRA-7731 (claude-2.1.309/reviewer-isolation.stdout.jsonl). The forwarded child input is only the prompt the parent wrote, so a subagent sees no producer context unless the parent copies it in.

single_agent.detail: With --tools Read,Edit,Write,Glob,Grep,Bash the init tools list has no Agent or Task tool, subagent_stats read spawned 0, and the model answered NO_AGENT_TOOL (claude-2.1.309/fresh-reader.stdout.jsonl, claude-2.1.309/plan-writer.stdout.jsonl). The tool is absent, so no-child execution is enforced, not instructed.

sol_ultra.detail: Claude has no ultra tier. claude --help lists --effort levels low, medium, high, xhigh, max. The CLI does not refuse the value: it prints a warning that it is ignoring an unknown --effort value, and runs at the default effort with exit 0. Evidence: claude-2.1.309/effort-ultra-ignored.stderr.txt, claude-2.1.309/effort-ultra-ignored.stdout.jsonl.

harnesses.tool_sandbox_constraints: No OS sandbox is in use. Workers run with --restricted --permission-mode acceptEdits, which confines the file tools to the workdir (a Write to ../outside.txt was refused, claude-2.1.309/restricted-writes.stdout.jsonl) and denies any command outside the allowlist (ls / was denied). acceptEdits alone did not confine a write (claude-2.1.309/acceptedits-outside-write.stdout.jsonl). Bash is limited to python and python3, and an allowed python3 -c call wrote ../outside2.txt outside the workdir, so a model-generated Python command can write anywhere the user can. The Claude sandbox setting failed every command on the probe host with 'nested userns is capability-restricted' (claude-2.1.309/sandbox-unavailable.stdout.jsonl) and is not used. Ambient context: CLAUDE.md, rules, memory, skills, and hooks listed as absent in an audit run (claude-2.1.309/ambient-audit.stdout.jsonl); the built-in system prompt and the account email and display name still load.
harnesses.failure_retry_behavior: A bad model id produced a result event with is_error true, subtype success, api_error_status 404, terminal_reason api_error, and the message text in result, and the process exited 1 (claude-2.1.309/invalid-model.stdout.jsonl). subtype stays success on an error, so the parser reads is_error and the result text. A usage-limit refusal was not captured; the committed usage-limit fixture is synthetic and copies the error shape above. No retry was observed. total_cost_usd is a notional list price on a subscription login, never a charge, and the runner does not read it.

effort_behavioral.prompt: A bag holds 7 red, 5 blue, and 3 green balls. Three balls are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that exactly two of the three share a color? Work it out carefully, then reply with the reduced fraction only. No tools.
